content.title: About
content.content: Sausage and peppers, no sauce is a dish made of sliced smoked or boiled sausage cooked together with sweet and hot peppers. It is served without tomato or cream sauces, so the main flavors come from the meat and aromatic spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originates from Italian cuisine, where sweet bell peppers and Italian sausage (salsiccia) are traditionally used.
Peppers add vitamin C and carotenoids, which enhance iron absorption from the meat.
It cooks quickly – about 10‑15 minutes over high heat.
Without sauce the dish is easier to control for calories and sugar content.
Sausage and peppers are often served as a side to pasta, rice, or potatoes.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Sausage provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Meat contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed, especially when paired with vitamin C from peppers.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Sausage supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from peppers
items.content: Sweet and hot peppers are rich in carotenoids and vitamin C, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: The combination of protein and vitamins helps strengthen the immune system.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed sausages often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Some sausages are high in saturated fat, which should be limited in cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Peppers may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Many sausages use nitrites and other preservatives that can be harmful in large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course, toss it with pasta, rice, couscous, or use it as a sandwich filling. Peppers can be cut into large chunks or thin strips according to personal preference.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Avoid freezing sausage with peppers if you plan to reheat, as the pepper texture may change.
